editorial:
If you love big family dramas with sharp dialogue and powerhouse acting, this one is for you. It follows the Weston family, whose members have scattered across the country but are forced back to their childhood home in Oklahoma after their father disappears. At the center is Violet, a sharp-tongued, pill-addicted mother played by Meryl Streep, who seems to enjoy tearing her daughters down. Julia Roberts, Julianne Nicholson, and Juliette Lewis play the three sisters, each carrying their own secrets and baggage. The vibe is tense, loud, and darkly funny, like a family reunion where everyone has something to hide.

The acting is the main draw. Streep and Roberts go toe-to-toe in intense dinner-table scenes, and the supporting cast, including Chris Cooper and Margo Martindale, is excellent. The downside is that it can feel heavy and exhausting, with so much shouting and pain that it may not be a fun watch for everyone. If you enjoy character-driven dramas with big emotions, this is a great pick. endingExplained: In the final scenes, the family secrets fully unravel. It is revealed that Little Charles, whom Ivy has been secretly dating, is actually her half-brother from an affair between Violet and her brother-in-law. Barbara, exhausted by her mother's cruelty and her own failing marriage, finally walks away and drives off, leaving Violet alone in the house with only the housekeeper Johnna. Violet stumbles around calling for her daughters, but no one comes back. The movie ends with Barbara on the road, free but broken, while Violet is left with nothing but her pills and her empty home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven family dramas with big emotions and powerhouse acting.
